data:
Tesla grew revenue 18.8% in fiscal 2023 to $96.8 billion, up from $81.5 billion in fiscal 2022, but profitability at the operating level moved the other way. Gross profit fell to $17.7 billion in fiscal 2023 from $20.9 billion in fiscal 2022, leaving a fiscal 2023 gross margin of 18.2%. Operating income dropped to $8.9 billion from $13.7 billion, for a fiscal 2023 operating margin of 9.2%. Part of the pressure reflects heavier investment, with R&D expense rising to $4.0 billion in fiscal 2023 from $3.1 billion in fiscal 2022. Even so, net income climbed 19.4% to $15.0 billion in fiscal 2023 from $12.6 billion, and diluted EPS rose to $4.30 from $3.62. The gap between falling operating income and rising net income points to items below the operating line, which investors should examine before treating fiscal 2023 earnings growth as recurring.

A note on the fact sheet: two stated ratios differ slightly from what the rounded inputs imply. $15.0 billion over $12.6 billion gives about 19.0% net income growth rather than 19.4%, and $17.7 billion over $96.8 billion gives about 18.3% gross margin rather than 18.2%. These gaps are most likely due to rounding in the underlying figures. I used the sheet's stated values as instructed, but you may want to check them against the source filings.
